key_insight: Instead of committing high-confidence tokens at scattered positions, commit the longest contiguous prefix of tokens that remain stable across diffusion steps (Longest Stable Prefix, LSP). This preserves KV-cache locality and avoids repeated expensive repairs, yielding faster and more coherent DLM inference.
problem_solved: Existing 'scattered acceptance' schedulers for Diffusion Language Models fracture the KV cache and memory locality, forcing repeated recomputation and repair across unstable token boundaries—leading to higher latency and degraded coherence.
method: Detect and commit the Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) of tokens that do not change across denoising/iteration steps, rather than accepting isolated high-confidence tokens at arbitrary positions.
Schedule decoding to preserve contiguous KV-cache use and memory locality, minimizing cache invalidations and repetitive forward passes for repaired token regions.
Design a hardware-aware scheduler that balances parallelism with contiguous commitment to reduce recomputation, lower memory bandwidth, and maintain output coherence.
impact: Practitioners can get substantially lower latency and improved text coherence from DLMs by using LSP-based schedulers—benefiting deployment on hardware-sensitive inference stacks (lower memory traffic, fewer recomputations, better throughput).
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: 'Scattered Acceptance' vs 'Longest Stable Prefix' showing token commitments and resulting KV-cache continuity.

paper_title: Beyond Scattered Acceptance: Fast and Coherent Inference for DLMs via Longest Stable Prefixes
paper_authors: Pengxiang Li, Joey Tsai, Hongwei Xue, Kunyu Shi, Shilin Yan
